item.title: AI May Have an Achilles Heel: Will Its Love of Money Deter Investors?
item.description: Everyone listened as Jensen Huang talked up AI and superchips. Then came CoreWeave.
item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: Susan Collins Is a Republican Unicorn
item.description: Susan Collins isn’t so much a US senator as she is a political unicorn.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: A French Accident Waiting to Happen
item.description: By certain numbers, France’s finances don’t look so bad. In euro-zone reality, there’s no room to maneuver.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Populism’s Next Chapter Is Being Written in Continental Europe
item.description: Since 2016, the story of populism in the rich world has been dominated by the Anglo-Saxons — by Britain’s vote for Brexit and America’s decision to elect Donald Trump not once (which might have been put down to naiveté) but twice. But things are about to change: Over the next year populism is likely to fade in the Anglo-Saxon world but burn ever brighter in continental Europe.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: AI Efficiencies Can Stifle Corporate Innovation
item.description: The latest way to sell artificial intelligence is with a high-tech version of the promise that corporate America last bought from Six Sigma. Earlier this month, Workday Inc. told investors that its customers should pay for its AI agents out of what they spend on labor and services, not just software. Workday itself, its CEO said, was looking to replace new hires with AI.
item.dc:creator: Gautam Mukunda

item.title: A Grad School Loan Should Reflect Your Wage Prospects
item.description: Our higher education system is broken. Families pay a fortune for degrees that do not pay off like they used to. However you feel about the future of advanced degrees, they’re certainly a mispriced asset — a mispricing that started in the market for student loans.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: Ukraine War: Vladimir Putin Is Happy to Pocket Trump’s Presents
item.description: Speaking near the Acropolis earlier this month, Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised the ancient Athenians who heroically repelled Persian invaders. The administration he serves is treating Ukraine’s resistance very differently.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Meta’s Muse Can’t Be a Freeloader’s Paradise Forever
item.description: When I introduced my mother to Uber, she asked whether it was always the same driver. Imagine that! Some poor guy waiting around all day on the off chance I’d need a car. Uber’s innovation, obviously, was to pair me with any available driver nearby. Only then was it economical — and it still took more than a decade for the idea to turn a profit.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: Factory Jobs in America Are Misunderstood and Overvalued
item.description: If there’s one thing on which American politicians can agree, it’s that US factory jobs are special. And with midterm elections approaching, the number of people working in manufacturing has become the scoreboard for President Donald Trump’s trade and industrial policies: Democrats point to 35,000 jobs lost since Trump took office in January 2025, while Republicans highlight a rebound of almost 60,000 since last December’s low.
item.dc:creator: Scott Lincicome

item.title: Healey Inherited a Better UK Budget Than He Thinks
item.description: John Healey’s job of presenting his first budget as chancellor of the Exchequer may not be enviable, but the one person he cannot blame is his predecessor. In terms of growth, fiscal consolidation and market sentiment, Rachel Reeves and former Prime Minister Keir Starmer left him a decent hand to play. The International Monetary Fund expects the British economy to expand by 1.3% this year, the second-fastest rate in the Group of Seven.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Kemi Badenoch Is Having a Great Time as the Latest Heir to Thatcher
item.description: If the worst job in British politics is leader of his majesty’s loyal opposition, nobody told Kemi Badenoch. Since becoming Conservative leader in 2024, months after the party’s worst election defeat, Badenoch has often had to put up with being eclipsed by Nigel Farage and his hard-right Reform UK. Her success in battling that is impressive.
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: Trump Should Reject Putin’s Plan for a Great Powers Summit
item.description: The mere prospect of Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump meeting for a great-powers summit while at the Asia Pacific Economic Community’s annual gathering next month is causing concern among America’s traditional allies, not to mention Ukraine. Rightly so.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Anthropic, Please Get on With Your IPO to Soothe the AI Trade
item.description: While the future is always uncertain, some market moments can feel sketchier than others. The wobble in the artificial intelligence trade reflects several near-term issues troubling investors, including elevated oil prices, rising interest rates, geopolitical anxiety and the imminent listing of AI behemoth Anthropic PBC. Some of these will get resolved sooner than others — but the latter will provide the acid test for sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Chris Hughes

item.title: AI Agents Are a Bigger Threat to Bank Deposits Than Stablecoins
item.description: Banks found it relatively easy to fend off the crypto bros. Artificial intelligence agents may prove a lot harder to tame.
item.dc:creator: Andy Mukherjee
